findings.title: Forgejo documents OAuth2 provider support with user consent
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider so third-party apps access resources with the user's consent. This applies to instance-wide OAuth2 apps on each customer's Forgejo instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth apps are registered by an instance administrator
findings.detail: Instance-wide OAuth2 applications must be created on the instance's /admin/applications page, so the customer instance administrator owns registration.
findings.appliesWhen: Any instance where the OAuth app is registered

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth tokens carry administrative rights and scopes are not implemented
findings.detail: The source says OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented and that third-party apps obtaining a user token have administrative rights. Least-privilege read-only access cannot be confirmed from the documentation.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

findings.title: Personal and scoped access token permissions do not apply to OAuth
findings.detail: The source says scoped tokens and personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2. Their read scopes must not be used as the OAuth grant for this app.

evidence.quote: Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;
see the Access Token scope section for more information.

findings.title: Repository search endpoint supports page and limit pagination
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search is the documented repository search route. The API returns page/limit pagination with Link headers and an x-total-count value.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

findings.title: Read-only repository scope for listing repositories
findings.detail: The requested listing is read-only, so the required grant is the read:repository scope, which covers GET routes. Write scopes are not required and must not be requested. OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented on this provider, so this scope cannot be enforced on an OAuth token and the grant should be treated as unenforced. Tokens obtained through this provider's OAuth2 flow have administrative rights, so the no-create/edit/delete prohibition must be enforced by the client, not by the grant.
findings.appliesWhen: The action lists repositories with the OAuth access model and requires read-only access.

steps.title: List repositories of the connected user with pagination
steps.detail: Call the authenticated user's repository listing with page and limit query parameters, using the OAuth access token as a Bearer token. Representative input: page=1, limit=30. Expected result: a JSON array of repository objects, with pagination in the Link header and total in x-total-count. Follow next links by incrementing page. Use GET only; never create, edit or delete repositories. Boundary check: send one GET with limit=50 and confirm at most 50 items; then send a GET with page beyond the total and confirm an empty array. Results list owned repositories only.
steps.doneWhen: Repository names are returned across pages, pagination is followed via the Link header or page parameter until no next page exists, and the boundary check confirms the page size cap and empty result beyond the last page using GET requests only.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register a test OAuth app on a test instance
On a test Forgejo instance where you are an instance administrator, create an OAuth2 application at /admin/applications and record the client ID, client secret and redirect URI. Leave other fields at defaults.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, REDIRECT_URI

Implement the authorize redirect, callback and token exchange
Build the authorization redirect with client ID, redirect URI, response_type=code and state. Implement the callback that receives the code and exchanges it at the access token endpoint. The redirect URI must match in both requests.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, REDIRECT_URI, STATE

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Authorize the test account and exchange the code
Done when: The test user approves consent and the callback returns an access token from the code exchange.

List repositories of the connected user with pagination
Done when: Repository names are returned across pages, pagination is followed via the Link header or page parameter until no next page exists, and the boundary check confirms the page size cap and empty result beyond the last page using GET requests only.

Test continuation to the next page until complete
Done when: Pages are collected until no rel=next link remains, and the total matches x-total-count.

Boundary check: confirm read-only requests on the granted access
Done when: The request log shows only GET calls from the test app and no repository write calls.
